name: aitp-console
//aitp: SDK floors that are load-bearing for THIS app, each with its consequence if violated -- same convention, and the same position, as `aitp-control-plane/package.json`'s `//aitp`: the rationale for a non-obvious version floor must live next to it or it is lost. This console is a *verifier*, never an issuer: the only two SDK symbols imported anywhere here are `verifyManifestJson` (`src/lib/api/verify-manifest.ts:1`) and `verifyRevocationList` (`src/lib/api/verify-revocation.ts:1`). A verifier does not choose what arrives on the wire, which is why this comment and CP's can reach different conclusions about the same release. `0.17.0` (current, PROTOCOL-LOAD-BEARING): strict `aitp/0.2` -> `aitp/0.3` cutover for Manifests and revocation snapshots. `verify_manifest` and `verify_revocation_list` check version before expiry and signature, so a `0.12`-`0.16` console reading a `0.17` CP (or the reverse) gets `version_unknown` on every artifact. That renders amber ('signature not assessed'), never red, and `src/test/sdk-verification.integration.test.ts` pins it (CUTOVER). The console therefore deploys together with `aitp-control-plane` (CP first, console minutes after), never alone. Signatures of `buildManifest` / `signRevocationList` / `verifyManifestJson` / `verifyRevocationList` are unchanged; `verifyEnvelope` / `signEnvelope` are new and deliberately not adopted (no envelopes reach the console). `0.15.0` (BEHAVIOURAL): both Node entry points now run the hardened wire parser before verifying (`wire::manifest` / `wire::revocation_snapshot`, `bindings/aitp-node/src/lib.rs:79-95`). A member outside the schema is now `unknown_field` (was `malformed` via serde `deny_unknown_fields` on `0.10.0`-`0.14.x`); a duplicate key is `malformed`; a revocation `entries[].jti` that is not UUID v4 is `malformed`. All three are pre-signature and classified amber at `src/lib/verification-display.ts` (`MANIFEST_UNASSESSED_CODES`, `REVOCATION_UNASSESSED_CODES`). Without that classification `unknown_field` falls through to a red 'VERIFICATION FAILED' -- an overclaim. `0.12.0` (historical floor, still true): fixes two false REJECTIONS only a verifier can hit. (1) `accepted_signature_algorithms` was not a member of `Manifest` until `0.12.0`, so on `0.10.0` an AUTHENTIC manifest carrying that spec-legal member threw `malformed` -- a false amber. (2) `Manifest::extensions` dropped a wire-present `"extensions":{}` from the signing input until fix `b78e608` made it `Option<ExtensionsMap>`, so on `0.10.0` such a manifest threw `signature_invalid` -- a RED badge on an authentic artifact. Evidence: `src/test/fixtures/minted-manifests.ts` (externally minted by `aitp-verifier-py`, re-minted for `aitp/0.3`). CP, an issuer building through `ManifestOpts`, cannot emit either shape, which is why CP did not treat `0.12.0` as load-bearing. `0.7.0` (historical floor): the first release where a `verifyManifestJson` failure carries a typed `.code`; `verify-manifest.ts` and `verify-revocation.ts` branch on `typeof code === 'string'`, and below this floor every failure would be misclassified as `sdk_unavailable`. READING RELEASE BOUNDARIES: `aitp-rs/CHANGELOG.md` now carries proper `## [0.12.0]` ... `## [0.16.0]` release headers (at tag `aitp-v0.17.0`, the 0.17 notes still sit under `## [Unreleased]`); git tags `aitp-vX.Y.Z` and npm agree from `aitp-v0.11.0` on (the old `aitp-v0.10.0` tag is NOT npm 0.10.0; that tree is `c7a7159`). Do not gate a bump on an `index.d.ts` diff: the behavioural changes above were invisible to it. RANGE CHOICE `^0.17.0`: on a 0.x range npm's caret pins the MINOR, so only `0.17.x` patches float and `0.18.0` needs a deliberate edit. This repo has no bump automation (CP has a `bump-aitp` workflow), so a caret here is a floor nobody automatically raises -- it drifted five minors (`0.12` -> `0.17`) before this bump. The lockfile, not the range, decides what is installed; the compensating control is this comment plus the `PROGRESS.md` entry.
